title: Risk control, not return chasing
objectives: Explain the price of risk control in plain words.
Answer “why rebalance if it can cost returns?”
body_md:
Rebalancing removes emotion from buying and selling decisions, and makes falls easier to sit through. It does not replace a review of the goal itself. A client who asks “why rebalance if it sometimes costs returns?” gets this answer: “Because you chose a risk level when things were calm. Rebalancing keeps that promise, even when markets tempt you to break it.”

> **Investor takeaway:** Rebalancing is a promise kept to the client's own risk choice.
example: Client: “Last time we rebalanced, equity kept rising.” Answer: “Rebalancing controls risk; it isn't a forecast. Some years it costs a little, some years it saves a lot.”
say: Rebalancing keeps the risk you chose.
Some years it costs a little, some years it saves a lot.

o: “Rebalancing keeps your risk at the level you chose; it doesn’t guarantee returns.”
